meta.parties: Periacaruppen Chettiar v. Messrs. Proprietors and Agents, Ltd., Et Al

rules.statement: A person who expends money or labour in improving property, intending to do so for his own benefit, thinking either that the property belongs to himself, or that he has a right to occupy it for some substantial period, whereas in fact he has no such right or title to the property and in consequence the improvements are acquired by the owner of the property, is entitled to claim from the latter the amount by which the property has been enhanced in value.
rules.supporting_quote: A person who expends money or labour in improving property, intending to do so for his own benefit, thinking either that the property belongs to himself, or that he has a right to occupy it for some substantial period, whereas in fact he has no such right or title to the property and in consequence the improvements are acquired by the owner of the property, is entitled to claim from the latter the amount by which the property has been enhanced in value. Even a person who has made improvements on another person's property mala fide , that is, knowing that ha had no title to the property, is entitled to claim the same measure of compensation if the owner stood by and allowed him to make the improvements without objection.
